title.value: Interactive Psychometrics for Autism With the Human Dynamic Clamp: Interpersonal Synchrony From Sensorimotor to Sociocognitive Domains
title.justification: The title is explicitly provided at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Interactive Psychometrics for Autism With the Human Dynamic Clamp: Interpersonal Synchrony From Sensorimotor to Sociocognitive Domains

analysis.description: This paper investigates the use of the Human Dynamic Clamp (HDC) as a psychometric instrument for assessing social abilities in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and neurotypical development. The study uses normative modeling and regression analyses to validate HDC's capacity to quantify interpersonal synchrony and its potential as a diagnostic marker for ASD.

type.justification: The paper involves conducting experiments with human participants using the Human Dynamic Clamp to analyze interpersonal synchrony in ASD, which is characteristic of empirical research.
type.quote: To study interpersonal synchrony with the HDC, we derived five standardized scores... Regression analyses were performed using normative modeling on global scores...

name.justification: The research field is focused on using computational models and systems, like the Human Dynamic Clamp, to examine psychiatric conditions, specifically autism.
name.quote: Keywords: computational psychiatry, human-machine interface (HMI), psychometric, interpersonal synchrony, autism spectrum disorder, coordination dynamics

name.justification: The study involves using a human-machine interface, specifically the Human Dynamic Clamp, to study interactions between humans and virtual avatars.
name.quote: The human dynamic clamp (HDC) is a human–machine interface designed on the basis of coordination dynamics for studying realistic social interaction under controlled and reproducible conditions.

name.justification: The study specifically investigates autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and how it affects social communication and motor skills.
name.quote: To study interpersonal synchrony with the HDC, we derived five standardized scores following a gradient from sensorimotor and motor to higher sociocognitive skills in a sample of 155 individuals (113 participants with ASD, 42 typically developing participants; aged 5 to 25 years; IQ > 70).

name.justification: The paper's focus on interpersonal synchrony and sociocognitive domains places it within the field of social cognition.
name.quote: Sociocognitive skills increased with developmental age while being affected by the ongoing task and HDC behavior.

name.justification: The Human Dynamic Clamp is explicitly mentioned as the core model/interface used in the study.
name.quote: The human dynamic clamp (HDC) is a human–machine interface designed on the basis of coordination dynamics for studying realistic social interaction under controlled and reproducible conditions.

is_contributed.justification: The paper emphasizes the validation and use of HDC as a novel method for studying interpersonal synchrony, suggesting it is a contribution.
is_contributed.quote: In this context, the human dynamic clamp (HDC) is a new paradigm of human–machine interaction based on the science of coordination (coordination dynamics) that enables the study of the neurobehavioral processes involved in IS.

is_executed.justification: The study involves conducting experiments with human participants, indicating the model was executed.
is_executed.quote: To study interpersonal synchrony with the HDC, we derived five standardized scores... using normative modeling on global scores according to four subconditions.

is_compared.justification: The paper includes comparative analysis of the HDC scores between different groups (ASD vs. typical development).
is_compared.quote: Comparative analysis between the two groups revealed a statistically significant decrease of the motor score in individuals with an ASD diagnosis compared with individuals with typical development.
